archetype.name: Playoff Team (slow-starting champion)
archetype.definition: A roster that won the title last season and still has the bones of a top-tier team, but whose first six games look like a middling one because its offense has not shown up yet.

report.headline: The defense and the glass travelled; the offense didn't. Expect it to return.
report.take:
The Knicks are 2-4, 17th on the site, with a Net Rtg of -0.7. That is a startling line for a team whose last season ended with 16 playoff wins and a 119.8 offensive rating that ranked 3rd. The split explains it. The defense is intact, with a 110 DRtg that ranks 10th. The offense has fallen off a cliff to a 109.3 ORtg, 20th, and 3.7 points per 100 below the league. This is not a team that forgot how to play. It is a good defensive team that has shot like a bad one for two weeks.

The shooting collapse is specific. Their 3P % (35.2) sits slightly above the league and their 3PA Rate is normal. The low FT Rate (24.5) is simply who they have always been, at 23.8 last season. What has cratered is finishing inside the arc. eFG % has gone from 55.7 last year to 49.5, 27th, and TS % from 59 to 53.1, 29th. Two players carry most of that. Jalen Brunson is using 32.1% of possessions at a 50.7 TS %. Mikal Bridges is at 41.1 TS %, which is most of why the wings grade an F. Karl-Anthony Towns, meanwhile, is 6th of 79 on the center tab with a 67.1 TS %, so the frontcourt offense is not the issue.

The record also flatters nobody, but it hasn't been fair either. The margin says 3 wins, not 2, and the losses were narrow: 100-106 and 93-98 to a 6-1 Philadelphia, 103-107 at a 5-1 Boston. That is a hard opening slate decided by a few possessions on cold shooting nights. What has held the floor up is rebounding. Their DRB % of 78.7 is 1st in the league and their ORB % is 6th, so opponents get one shot and the Knicks often get two. The defense doesn't force turnovers (Opp TOV % 26th), so it wins by finishing possessions instead of stealing them. That style is stable.

The direction from here is up. Shooting this far below a multi-year baseline, with the same core, regresses. A defense built on rebounding and rim protection (Opp Rim FG % 62.5 against a 65.3 league mark) does not. Six games is a small sample, and the on-off numbers in it are noisy. Anunoby at -38.1 and Bridges at -32.1 should not be read as verdicts yet.

strengths.title: Best defensive rebounding in the league
strengths.body: They grab 78.7% of opponents' misses, 1st in the league and well above the 72.6 average, while also ranking 6th on the offensive glass. Towns, with 81 rebounds, and Drummond in his minutes anchor it. Last season's 76.7 DRB % shows this is a habit of the roster rather than a six-game blip, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Defense holding up without turnovers
strengths.body: A 110 DRtg ranks 10th and sits 3.1 points per 100 better than the league. They get there by limiting the rim (Opp Rim FG % 62.5, 11th) and ending possessions on the glass rather than forcing mistakes. Points allowed per game rank 6th, helped by a slow pace. This is a structurally sound defense and should stay top-12.

strengths.title: Towns is carrying the efficiency
strengths.body: Towns sits 6th of 79 on the center tab with a 67.1 TS %, a 3.4 BPM and 131 points. That is the one part of the offense performing at last season's level. It makes the frontcourt grade a B- even with Anunoby's rough start.

concerns.title: Offense shooting far below its baseline
concerns.body: TS % has fallen from 59 last season to 53.1, 29th, and eFG % from 55.7 to 49.5. The drop comes from inside the arc, since 3P % is still above the league. That points to cold finishing more than a broken scheme. It is the main reason a 3rd-ranked offense now sits at a 109.3 ORtg, and it is the likeliest thing to regress back up.

concerns.title: Brunson and Bridges in a slump
concerns.body: Brunson is using 32.1% of possessions at a 50.7 TS %, which drags a heavy share of the offense down with him. Bridges is the only real wing, and his 41.1 TS % and -5.3 BPM are why the wings grade is an F. One player decides that whole grade. Both are six-game samples, but the wing grade won't move until Bridges does.

concerns.title: No pressure on the ball
concerns.body: An Opp TOV % of 12.1 ranks 26th, so the defense rarely creates easy offense. With a halfcourt attack this cold, that leaves almost no transition cushion, especially at a 97.9 pace. It is a style trait that is unlikely to change, but it matters less once the shots fall.

trend.note: The margin has hovered near even all season, while the record has swung on close games: three losses to open, two wins, then a 93-98 loss in Philadelphia. The last five games run slightly better than the season as a whole.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games against 1-5 teams, then a real test in Cleveland
weekAhead.body:
After an opening run that included 6-1 Philadelphia twice and 5-1 Boston, the schedule softens sharply. Brooklyn and Chicago both come to New York at 1-5. Brooklyn's offense ranks 28th in ORtg, and Chicago's 121.8 DRtg ranks 27th. Those are exactly the games a cold-shooting offense should use to find its rhythm. The Knicks already beat Chicago 133-127 on the road.

The week closes at Cleveland, 7th on the site, with a 117.2 ORtg and an A+ frontcourt. That is the barometer game. Two wins at home are the expectation, and a split of the week's final game would put them back at .500.

keyMatchups.title: Brunson against Chicago's porous guards
keyMatchups.body: Chicago lets point guards score 29.67 points a game, 10.04 above their own averages, the 29th-ranked mark against the position. It also allows a 39.3 Opp 3P %, 28th. If Brunson's shooting is going to turn, this is the night, and Chicago's 106.2 pace means extra possessions to do it with.

keyMatchups.title: Attacking Brooklyn's soft rim
keyMatchups.body: Brooklyn allows 71% at the rim, 26th. Power forwards are scoring 32.83 points a game against them, 28th. That is the matchup for Anunoby to break out of his -3.2 BPM start and for the Knicks to fix their finishing problem. Brooklyn's elite defensive glass (DRB % 2nd) will make second chances scarce, though.

keyMatchups.title: Towns against Cleveland's frontcourt
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's frontcourt grades A+ and its Opp Rim FG % ranks 4th, so the paint is closed. Yet centers score 22.67 points a game against the Cavaliers, 6.56 over their averages and 29th against the position, with the most threes allowed to the spot. A stretch big like Towns is the answer. Brunson has the harder side of it: Cleveland holds point guards to 18.17 points, 4th.

weekAhead.watch: Whether team TS % climbs out of the bottom two against Brooklyn's and Chicago's defenses; if it doesn't against these two, the slump is more than noise.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense and rebounding look real and repeatable. The offense is running about ten points per 100 below what this core produced last season, mostly on two-point finishing and two slumping regulars. That gap closes as the sample grows. The current pace of 27 wins reflects a hard schedule and close losses, not the team's level. A rebound to something like a 113 to 117 ORtg, paired with a top-12 defense, makes this a comfortable playoff team in the 45 to 51 win range again.

The ceiling depends on the wings. With Bridges the only real contributor at small forward and grading an F, the Knicks need him back near his usual level to look like a contender rather than a solid playoff side. A sustained Brunson slump at his usage would cap them at the lower end.

confidence.note: Six games, against a tough slate; the strong history of this core points to regression.
